findings.reason: diff.patch removes invalidXRangeOrder and its early `return comp`. In range.js:405-424, xM now carries into xm/xp and returns '*', and range.js:462-463 returns `>=M.0.0 <M+1.0.0-0` when xm is set, so the concrete trailing numbers are dropped and nothing rejects them.
findings.claim: With the invalidXRangeOrder guard deleted, out-of-order X-ranges like x.1.2 or 1.x.2 are silently widened to '*' or '>=1.0.0 <2.0.0-0'.
findings.evidence: The diff deletes `invalidXRangeOrder` (`(isX(M) && !isX(m)) || (isX(m) && p && !isX(p))`) and its guard `if (invalidXRangeOrder(M, m, p)) { return comp }` from `replaceXRange`. The callback now goes straight to `const xM = isX(M)`. When xM is set and there is no `>`/`<`, it returns `ret = '*'` (line 424). When `xm` is set it returns `>=${M}.0.0 <${+M + 1}.0.0-0` (line 463). The concrete minor and patch numbers after the wildcard are dropped without any error.

findings.reason: diff.patch touches only classes/range.js. A grep of test/ for x.N.N, 1.x.N and *.N patterns found no matches, so neither the old rejection nor the new widening is tested.
findings.claim: No test covers the changed behavior for out-of-order X-ranges.
findings.evidence: diff.patch only touches `classes/range.js`, removing 9 lines. A search of `test/` (including `test/fixtures/range-parse.js`, `range-include.js`, `range-exclude.js`) finds no fixtures shaped like `x.N.N`, `*.N` or `N.x.N`, so neither the old rejection nor the new wildcard result is covered.
